assumptions.obligation: No request (i_a_valid = 0) while rst_ni is asserted
TL-UL host rule: once i_a_valid is 1 and o_a_ready is 0, i_a_valid stays 1 and all A-channel fields (opcode, param, size, source, address, mask, data, instr, intg_flip) stay stable
Requests at offset 0x200 and above are not used
Each new request uses an a_source that is not outstanding (a source is free again once its response is taken in the same cycle)
The combined full-word ALERT_TEST write (fatal_fault = 1 with regwen = 0, e.g. 0x0000_0001) is not used; tests write 0x8000_0001

Effective full-word writes (a_size = 2, mask 0xF, good integrity, data access) to CFG0, TIMER_V_LOWER0 and TIMER_V_UPPER0 happen only while CTRL.active_0 = 0. The shadow of CTRL is updated only by such effective writes

notes: CHK-008 not added: the rules don't oblige the test bench to stay idle in the first cycle after reset release. RT-8-29 (read with RT-8-30 and RT-8-31) covers only the time rst_ni is low, which ENV-01 already assumes. RT-2-03 and CP-T1.5.2-04 only say release is synchronous, and TL-T3.1.3.1-02 says devices tolerate short reset windows. 'D-016' is not in the given specification text. The trace is a legal stimulus, so it is a real finding or a problem in CHK-008 itself (a check that asserts a DUT input is suspect); it should go back to the checker owner. CHK-004's step-1 trace is legal for the same reason. Other triage suggestions not added: (a) non-contiguous masks: TL-T3.1.3.4-02 is only a 'should not' for hosts, RT-4.1-05 explicitly allows bad-mask requests as legal stimulus, and RT-4.1-06 and TL-T3.1.3.5-03/04 require d_error = 1. (b) banning data 0x00000001 at every mask and size: per RG-T1.4.1-05 a sub-word write is an error with no effect, so it is not the combined write of RT-8-15; if the DUT wrongly carries one out, that is a bug to catch. (c) byte-write CTRL tracking: these must fail with no effect (RG-T1.4.1-05, RT-8-19), so the shadow ignores them. (d) a pending CTRL write cannot occur: the A channel takes one request per cycle (TL-T2.2-03) and the shadow updates at the handshake. Change made: the CTRL.active_0 shadow and ENV-08 now also require a_size = 2. Otherwise a PutFullData with mask 0xF and the wrong size, which must be rejected (TL-T3.1.3.4-04, TL-T3.1.3.5-02/03), could move the shadow away from the real register and allow CFG0/TIMER_V writes while the timer is active. Nothing was run.
